solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Animals whose food is superior to other animals

definitions.text: Animals whose food is superior to other animals

parts.words: Animals whose food is superior to other animals
parts.note: superior is read literally as higher up: these tall browsers eat leaves from treetops that other beasts cannot reach

explanation.surface: A boast that some creatures dine on finer fare than the rest of the animal kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior' looks like a judgement of quality; it means physically higher, the treetop leaves only the tallest animals can reach.
explanation.definitionFit: These long-necked African animals browse on high foliage, food literally above that of other grazers.

clue.text: Like a well-drilled army that's on foot

definitions.meaning: soldiers who march in perfect unison are keeping step together
the arched upper part of the foot, between toes and ankle

explanation.surface: A drill sergeant praises troops marching smartly on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means marching in unison; as one word it names the arch of the foot.

clue.text: Shrink from hunting initially with wild boar around

indicators.note: around says the rearranged boar letters sit on either side of the picked letter
wild suggests the letters of boar run riot into a new order
initially tells us to take only the opening letter of hunting

explanation.surface: Someone recoils from the hunt when an angry boar circles them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns BOAR into ABOR, and 'around' puts H (from 'hunting initially') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to recoil from it in loathing, a strong synonym of shrinking away.

clue.text: Stout friends, about 50, who share digs

indicators.note: about means the word for stout goes around the numeral

parts.note: stout means fat
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
mates are friends

explanation.surface: A pair of tubby middle-aged pals live together in shared lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digs' is British slang for rented lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Housemates who rent a flat together are those sharing lodgings, digs being informal British for rooms.

clue.text: Stay faithful

definitions.meaning: to stop a flow, especially of blood, as in stemming a wound
loyal and steadfast, as a firm supporter

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning to stem a flow and an adjective meaning steadfastly loyal.

clue.text: What many, in panic, make themselves

definitions.text: What many, in panic, make themselves

parts.words: What many, in panic, make themselves
parts.note: frightened people run off and vanish, completing the idiom about making oneself hard to find

explanation.surface: A description of how crowds behave when panic strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'make yourself scarce' means leave quickly or disappear.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for fleeing out of sight completes the sentence: people make themselves rare by bolting.

clue.text: Boat causes waters to rise

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: pools are bodies of water

explanation.surface: A vessel makes the water level climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rise' in a down answer reads POOLS upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-masted sailing vessel is a kind of boat.

clue.text: Special among men, a legendary Greek hero

indicators.note: special in the sense of specially made up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: One mythical warrior stands out among his fellow fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special' rearranges the nine letters of AMONG MEN A; the 'a' that seems to belong to the definition is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The king of Mycenae who led the Greeks at Troy is a hero of Greek legend.

clue.text: Giant firm states no profit is taken

indicators.note: is taken (in) means the word for no profit goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
US is the United States
a loss is the absence of profit

explanation.surface: A huge American company reports that it made no profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is taken' marks an insertion: the word for no profit is taken in between the firm and the states.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient bronze statue at Rhodes gave its name to anything huge, so it means a giant.

clue.text: Spasmodic trouble for our airways

parts.note: airways sounds like airline routes, but here means the breathing passages that go into spasm

explanation.surface: Something fitful is disrupting the national airline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our airways' suggests an airline; it means the body's bronchial tubes.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronic condition where the bronchial passages tighten in spasms, making breathing difficult.

clue.text: Lovely girl, outwardly competent

indicators.note: outwardly means the word for competent is on the outside

parts.note: able means competent
Dora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A charming young woman who also seems capable on the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' marks the word for competent as the outside piece, with the girl's name tucked inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adorable is delightful and charming, so lovely in the sense of sweet.

clue.text: The offer of money may make him cross

definitions.text: The offer of money may make him cross

parts.words: The offer of money may make him cross
parts.note: cross means go over water, not angry: a fare paid gets the boatman to row you over

explanation.surface: A man who gets angry when someone tries to bribe him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like annoyed; it means to make a crossing, as a boatman does for a fare (Charon in myth needed a coin).
explanation.definitionFit: A boatman paid a fare to carry passengers across a river or strait.

clue.text: Oral entreaties find favour

indicators.note: oral means spoken, so we want a word that is pronounced like the plural of the requests

parts.note: pleas are entreaties

explanation.surface: Spoken requests win approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oral' signals the spoken form: PLEAS said out loud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To please is to give satisfaction or be liked, the same as finding favour with someone.

clue.text: Receive notice of termination and become agitated

definitions.meaning: to be told something is being wound up, read literally
the British idiom for becoming nervous or frightened

explanation.surface: Being sacked leaves a worker anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom, chiefly British, means to grow alarmed; literally it could mean being told of a winding-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally being informed of a winding-up, and idiomatically growing anxious or scared.

clue.text: Celebrity seen in Sergeant's Mess

indicators.note: mess means a muddle, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters are taken including the s

explanation.surface: A famous figure is spotted in the military dining hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess' looks like the soldiers' dining room; it signals that the nine letters of SERGEANTS are muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Fame or eminence; celebrity in the sense of being renowned rather than a famous person.

clue.text: Two wines favoured in York

parts.note: white is one kind of wine
rosé is another kind of wine

explanation.surface: A pair of wines is popular in a northern English city.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of York's emblem in the Wars of the Roses was this flower; it remains Yorkshire's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: This flower was the badge of the House of York and is still Yorkshire's emblem.

clue.text: Flat delivery on an even pitch

definitions.meaning: speech given without any rise and fall in the voice
a single unvarying note, as an adjective

explanation.surface: Describing a dull speaker who never varies their tone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a dull unvaried manner of speaking and also a sound held at one steady pitch.

clue.text: A pit owner's to arrange for a source of energy

indicators.note: arrange tells us to put these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A colliery proprietor must organise a supply of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrange' shuffles the twelve letters of A PIT OWNERS TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that generates electricity is a source of energy for the grid.

clue.text: A classical way to gain height as a flier

parts.note: via is Latin for road or way
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A traditional route for gaining altitude when flying.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOR is a rocky hilltop on English moorland such as Dartmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot of an aircraft is a flier in the sense of one who flies.

clue.text: Suffer having to change rig with first mate

indicators.note: to change asks for the letters of rig to be put in another order

parts.note: Eve was the first wife, Adam's mate in Genesis

explanation.surface: A sailor has a hard time refitting the rigging alongside the ship's first officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' turns RIG into GRI. 'First mate' suggests a ship's officer; it is Eve, the first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To grieve is to feel deep sorrow, which is to suffer distress.

clue.text: Embryo to fuse together somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are combined in some unspecified order

explanation.surface: Two cells combine somehow to begin new life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges TO FUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An unborn offspring in the womb; strictly the later stage after the embryo, but used broadly.

clue.text: An MP must do so before he can sit

definitions.text: An MP must do so before he can sit

parts.words: An MP must do so before he can sit
parts.note: a candidate must offer themselves for election before taking a seat in Parliament

explanation.surface: A joke that a politician has to get up before sitting down.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a candidate stands for Parliament; once elected, an MP sits for a constituency.
explanation.definitionFit: British usage: one offers oneself as a candidate before being elected to a seat.

clue.text: Clumsy former spouse in Pinter play

indicators.note: in puts the former partner inside the rearranged name
play suggests the letters of the dramatist's name move about

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife

explanation.surface: An ex-husband gives a bungling performance in a Harold Pinter drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' rearranges PINTER to INPERT; 'in' then places the former spouse within that, after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inexpert lacks skill, so they are clumsy or bungling.

clue.text: Indicate position in field

definitions.meaning: to show by aiming a finger
a cricket fielding position on the off side near the batsman

explanation.definitionFit: A verb for showing with a finger, and the name of a cricket fielding position square of the batter.

clue.text: Prophetic warning shout to players

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shout to warn of a ball in flight
the cast is the set of actors in a show

explanation.surface: A soothsayer calls out a caution to a team.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is shouted on a golf course to warn people a ball is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast is a prediction of what will happen, a warning given in advance.

clue.text: Fifty-one in surplus — yet he wanted more

indicators.note: in puts the numeral inside the word for surplus

parts.note: over means in excess, surplus
LI is fifty-one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Despite having a surplus of fifty-one, someone still craves more.
explanation.walkthrough: The orphan in Dickens's Oliver Twist famously asks for more gruel.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's workhouse orphan famously asked for a second helping of gruel.

clue.text: Well acquainted with the metric system

definitions.meaning: knowledgeable and practised, as in skilled in a subject
metric here means poetic metre, so written in verse form

explanation.definitionFit: It means skilled or knowledgeable, and also cast in verse, the system of poetic metre.

clue.text: X-ray unit

parts.note: a unit measuring exposure to ionising radiation, named after the German physicist who discovered the rays

explanation.surface: A hospital radiology department.
explanation.definitionFit: The old unit of radiation exposure, named after Wilhelm Röntgen, discoverer of X-rays.
